fix: In stages/evaluation.py:_shrinkage (~line 448) and explore_previews.py:447-450, word the offer and caption by the slope's side of 1 (or withhold the offer when slope_of returns a slope >= 1), so 'Shrink' and 'each risk moves toward the mean' are never shown for an expansion; and name in the offer that the out-of-fold slope comes from (K-1)/K-row fold models and shrinks somewhat more than the bootstrap's.
evidence: The method itself is the standard, sourced update (Collins 2024, Van Houwelingen & le Cessie 1990), offered opt-in (UpdatingSpec default 'none', decisions.py:1785), with the bootstrap slope used by default below 20,000 units; both referees agree it improves calibration on average, so referee A's small-n noise objection (Riley 2021) is a caveat for any shrinkage, not an app error. What is actually wrong is narrow, as the audit found: no guard when the slope exceeds 1 (then the coefficients expand under a 'Shrink' label and a 'toward the mean' caption), and the out-of-fold fallback over-shrinks a little, which both referees accept; it is labeled, and B's simulation shows it still beats no update.

fix: Stop prepending the linear family's inference._cluster_concerns (inference.py:638-649) at ordinal.py:377; give the ordinal table its own lines that say CR1 with G/(G-1) on t(G-1), Cameron & Miller's stated minimum that still over-rejects with few or unequal units, and below FEW_CLUSTERS (30) either flag the intervals as possibly too narrow or add a few-cluster method (a CR2-type correction or wild cluster score bootstrap), with a coverage test at G = 8-30 with unequal units.
evidence: Running ordinal_table with G = 12 shows the caption 'sandwich ... G/(G-1) correction ... on t(11)' beside concern lines saying 'cluster-robust (CR2, G = 12)' and 'the intervals use the CR2 small-sample correction with Bell-McCaffrey degrees of freedom, which Cameron & Miller recommend when clusters are few', so for every ordinal table with 8-29 units the user is told a method and df that were not used, the very correction the source recommends for this case. Both referees agree, and their simulations concur, that CR1 + t(G-1) undercovers (about 80-88%) with unequal units or exposure in few units; I accept that, and the audit's reading of Cameron & Miller ('at a minimum'). The independent-rows Wald part is fine.

fix: No behavior change; relabel the comment at materiality.py:103-104 as the app's surfacing convention for when the finding line appears (not BLUEPRINT §14 rule 1's nutrient-recognizer rule), and add a test that the energy_adjustment question is still asked at |r| < 0.3.
evidence: The energy-model question is a Router Decide (quest.py:172) whose applicability (interview.py:278-299) depends only on the dietary lens, an energy-role column and an exposure, never on r; called directly it applies with no data at all. So below 0.3 the substitution-versus-addition choice is still asked, and only the extra noticing line is absent. The app's own docstring (materiality.py:652-654) says the meaning changes at any r, so the referees' point is right about the inventory's wording, but their bite ('suppresses the energy-model decision') does not happen.

fix: None needed; optionally have the quintile option's confounder-role text at exposure_form.py:1070-1073 say that five groups leave some residual confounding, as the categories option already says for three or fewer.
evidence: The app recommends the spline, marks the straight line only 'available' with the conditional 'Sound when the relation is close to a line; a curve it misses biases the slope' (exposure_form.py:1058-1061), and marks quintiles 'rank_lower' for the sourced reasons of lost within-fifth variation and a step at each cut (Bennette & Vickers 2012; Greenland 1995). So referee A's worry that a U-shaped response is steered to a straight line does not hold, because the spline that handles curvature leads and the line's text names its failure. Referee B and the audit are right that the ranking is a labeled ruling with sourced reasons.

fix: At case_control.py:200-204 (and the docstring at :48-53) replace 'This is a limit of the design, not a missing feature' with 'these sets alone cannot give risks: that needs external incidence by the matching factors (an attributable-risk model, as in Gail et al. 1989) or, for sets nested in a known cohort, its risk-set sizes (Langholz & Borgan 1997), which TurboTab does not yet take', and cite conditional-likelihood theory (Breslow & Day 1980) instead of Janes & Pepe 2008 for the intercept argument.
evidence: Both referees and the audit agree, and I accept, that the two mechanisms are right for these data alone, so refusing inside the app is defensible. But absolute risk is estimable from matched designs with external incidence or cohort sampling information, so 'a limit of the design, not a missing feature' is false, and the cited Janes & Pepe 2008 is about classification accuracy, not risk. Since the refusal is correct for the data the app holds and only its stated scope and reason are wrong, this is S2, not S1.

fix: Stop withholding at stages/causal.py:740-746 for a numeric exposure when variation().violated (models/causal.py:1159-1183); report the cross-fitted R² as a precision note (the residual SD and the sqrt(VIF) widening, already in the interval), remove 'Positivity is practically violated ... extrapolates where x barely varies' from the methods sentence (core/causal.py:791-797) and 'revisit the adjustment set' from _variation_reason (stages/causal.py:584-588), and if a continuous-exposure positivity check is wanted, base it on support of the residual at the contrasted values, with a known-truth test.
evidence: My simulation (DML-PLR, OLS nuisances that are correctly specified, n = 300, 500 reps) gave cross-fitted R² 0.95 with bias +0.005 and coverage 0.95, and R² 0.99 with bias +0.02 and coverage 0.94: high R² only widens the interval, as both referees say (Frisch-Waugh), yet the app returns a 409, withholds the estimate until the user records that 'positivity is practically violated', and writes that into the methods sentence. With random-forest nuisances (the default from 500 rows), the real hazard of amplified misfit bias showed (bias -0.09 to -0.12, coverage 0.53-0.67), but there the cross-fitted R² stayed at 0.86-0.88, below the 0.9 line, so the gate does not catch the problem it is said to catch. Its only source is Kutner's collinearity rule of thumb, which the audit confirms says nothing about positivity.

fix: None to the code; restate the inventory claim as the audit's corrected statement (under the population answer the scores follow the design, whole PSUs within strata and weighted losses, per Wieczorek, Guerin & McMahon 2022), dropping the 'only if'.
evidence: The app's text (plan_previews.py:1518-1546; the design_cv.py docstring) says only that under the population answer the cross-validation follows the design and every score is weighted, and that under the sample answer the unweighted scores are 'the procedure's performance on these n rows, not the surveyed population's'. Both are faithful to WGM 2022 and the surveyCV construction. Referee A's objection (design-based CV is sufficient, not necessary, when weights are non-informative) targets the inventory's 'only if', which the app never states; the app applies the method by the user's estimand answer, which is defensible.

fix: In readings.unit_day_candidates (readings.py:866, 884-887) use the kcal pass band's multiplicative tolerance (0.90-1.10 times factor x days) for kJ x N and kcal x N as well, so a kJ file with the reconstruction error the kcal band already tolerates keeps kJ among the offered readings; add a c2 case at a kJ reconstruction ratio of 0.94 and of 1.07.
evidence: The settle rule is safe, and every referee and the audit agree: only [('kcal', 1)] settles, so nothing is settled wrongly. Referee A's asymmetry is real: probing unit_day_candidates, a 1-day kJ file at a reconstruction ratio of 0.93-0.95 is offered only 'kcal over 4 days', and one at 1.06 is offered nothing. But the ask keeps an 'Another unit or day count' exit (decisions.py:3711-3720), and kJ read as a 4-day kcal total misstates daily energy by only 4.184/4, about 4.6%, not the factor of 4.184 A states. Referee B's two-macronutrient case does not arise in my probe: protein + fat alone hits the drift gate ('the macronutrients do not reconstruct it'), with no spurious 2-day reading.

fix: Under Predict, make materiality.collinear_label (materiality.py:957-958) return For the record (or Confirm, as calm/BEATS_PREDICT M4 has it) and change _collinear_lever (stages/explore.py:666-674) to recommend 'keep both; a penalized family shrinks on its own; importance read grouped', dropping 'the penalty spreads the weight' from the elastic-net option, since set_selection elastic_net is a selection filter put before every family (pipeline.py:783), not a penalty in the fitted model.
evidence: Both referees are right that a |r| >= 0.9 pair does not harm in-distribution prediction, so a Decide 'regardless of materiality' has no basis, and the audit notes it contradicts the app's own Predict beats and its selection menu, which ranks 'none' soundest. The bite is worse than either referee found: the Decide's recommended answer is the elastic-net selector applied to every family. In my simulation (n = 500, a pair at r = 0.95, one U-shaped predictor) it kept both collinear predictors in 10 of 10 runs, so nothing was shared, left OLS unchanged (MSE 6.14 vs 6.14), and raised the random forest's test MSE from 2.26 to 4.17 by dropping the nonlinear predictor half the time.

fix: Reword SINGLE_SPLIT at teaching/content.py:91-96 to 'For regression-type models below about 20,000 units, bootstrap optimism correction is the recommended default and repeated cross-validation is acceptable; tree ensembles keep their cross-validated score, since the bootstrap overstates them; a single split is the weakest option', citing Steyerberg et al. 2001 and Coley et al. 2023 beside the pack.
evidence: Both referees' simulations (random forest: bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.94-0.95 against a true 0.63-0.68) are right about the method, but the app already acts on it: random_forest, boosted_trees and xgboost all declare bootstrap_optimism = False and keep their cross-validated score, and the bootstrap option carries BOOTSTRAP_CAUTION (validation.py:330-332). So the referees' bite (a grossly optimistic score on the seal card) does not happen. What remains is a teaching card stating an unconditional rule that the app's own practice limits to regression-type families below RESAMPLE_BELOW: a scope fix, not a wrong number.

fix: Change the imputed_copies option text at teaching/content.py:541-543 to 'under inference each copy is analyzed and the estimates pooled by Rubin's rules; combining them is recorded as a limitation', and gate the pooled wording at voice.py:2085-2088 on stages.modeling.imputed_copies_column(state) being non-None, falling back to the not-pooled sentence otherwise.
evidence: Both referees are right, and the R parity test (mitools::MIcombine and mice::pool.scalar to 1e-6) confirms it: when the copy column is named and each copy is kept as a record, the engine pools by Rubin's rules as NCHS directs. Two texts misstate this, as the audit found. The teaching option says copies are 'under inference kept only as a recorded limitation', the opposite of what the fit does. The methods sentence claims pooling whenever purpose is inference and it is unacknowledged, while imputed_copies_column (modeling.py:1462-1472) pools only with implicate_column set and unit 'row'. The behavior is right; the wording needs fixing.

evidence: Both referees find the three-tier wording sound, and I agree.
